description:
FILED s473x (2026-09-19) as the RESIDUE of round 34's integer fast path, so it
is not re-derived and not attempted blind.

WHAT SHIPPED.  `%p-plain-integer-string` answers an optionally-signed run of
ASCII digits with a digit loop; every other shape answers NIL and takes
`parse-perl-number`'s general body unchanged.  That body still, for a DECIMAL
or an EXPONENT string:

  1. allocates a `string-left-trim` copy;
  2. allocates a `string-downcase` OF THE WHOLE STRING and a
     `string-right-trim` of that -- both only to test for inf/nan;
  3. runs ~12 `subseq`+`string=` probes for the inf/nan spellings;
  4. scans the numeric extent by hand;
  5. `subseq`s the extent;
  6. calls `read-from-string` -- the full CL READER, with a string input
     stream (%init-string-input-stream, %read-preserving-whitespace,
     read-token, make-integer).

Two independent pieces, and they are NOT the same difficulty:

(a) CHEAP AND SAFE: steps 1-3 can be gated on ONE character test.  Only a
    string whose first non-sign character is `i`, `I`, `n`, `N` or `1` can be
    an inf/nan spelling (inf, infinity, nan, nanq, nans, qnan, snan, 1.#inf*,
    1.#nan*, 1.#ind*, 1#inf*, 1#nan*, 1#ind*, and `q`/`s` for the bare qnan /
    snan).  Everything else can skip the downcase, the right-trim and the
    twelve probes and go straight to the extent scan.  The `q`/`s` spellings
    make the admissible set {i I n N 1 q s}.  Contained, and it keeps the
    general body as the one decider.

(b) NOT SAFE WITHOUT A PROOF: replacing `read-from-string` for a DECIMAL.  The
    answer must be the SAME DOUBLE, bit for bit -- a hand-rolled
    mantissa/scale loop is not, in general, correctly rounded, and PCL has
    already been bitten by "close enough" float arithmetic (#1514's divide
    needed an exact-representability argument before it could take the IEEE
    path; #1515 records what happens when the two sides round differently).
    If anyone takes it: the bar is a byte-compare of `read-from-string` against
    the replacement over a large random corpus AND the boundary set
    (subnormals, 17-significant-digit round-trips, 1e308, 5e-324, exponents
    near the +/-400 cutoffs the existing body checks).

WHAT IT IS WORTH.  Not measured on its own.  After the integer path,
`parse-perl-number` no longer appears above 2 % in any bench row profiled in
round 34 -- `ovlsub` was its one big customer and is now +29.5 %.  So this is
for a program that numifies FLOAT-shaped strings in a loop (a CSV or JSON
reader over decimals), and there is no bench row for that today.  ADD THE ROW
FIRST: the round-34 rule is that a lever is taken only against a row it can be
measured on.
subject: PERF residue of round 34: parse-perl-number still runs a `string-downcase` of the whole string and the CL READER for a DECIMAL -- (a) the inf/nan probes can be gated on one character, (b) replacing read-from-string for a float needs a bit-for-bit proof; needs a bench row first
